title: Sync cursor can advance past unobserved feed changes
reasoning: The route returns a wall-clock server_timestamp for the client's next cursor before it has read the change set, while the incremental queries include any row whose updated_at/deleted_at is greater than the previous cursor. A concurrent writer can set updated_at or deleted_at before this timestamp, remain uncommitted while the route queries, then commit after the query. The client stores the returned server_timestamp and the committed change has a timestamp <= that cursor, so future calls filtered by updated_at/deleted_at > since will never return it.
reproduction: Start with client cursor T0. In one transaction, update a Feed and set updated_at=T1, but delay commit. During that delay, call GET /api/feeds/changes?since=T0 so line 88 returns S where S > T1, and the queries do not see the uncommitted row. Commit the writer transaction. The next GET /changes?since=S excludes the row because T1 is not greater than S.
recommendation: Make the sync cursor reflect the visible data snapshot rather than an unconstrained wall-clock timestamp. For example, advance it only to the max updated_at/deleted_at value actually observed, or introduce a committed change sequence/version and return that as the cursor. Add an upper bound to the query if returning a high-water mark.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/test_feeds.py does not call GET /api/feeds/changes and has no concurrent or cursor advancement scenario.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that simulates a feed update timestamped before the returned cursor but committed after the route's read, then verifies a later sync still receives that change or that the cursor did not advance past it.
minimumFixScope: app/api/feeds.py cursor generation/query bounds, plus focused tests for incremental sync cursor safety.
